query: How can clinics improve triage and scheduling?

per_column.name: clinical_urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Clinical urgency is a patient-intrinsic driver of both how a case is triaged/scheduled and the efficiency outcome; it is a common cause, not a settable lever. It largely restates the existing 'urgency' column rather than introducing an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: chief_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: The nature of the complaint influences both triage assignment and scheduling efficiency; an immutable case attribute, not something a clinic can set.

per_column.name: presentation_acuity_type
per_column.rationale: Acute vs chronic/preventive presentation is an intrinsic case characteristic that drives both triage routing and efficiency; not intervenable.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_required
per_column.rationale: Ordering imaging/labs lies on the pathway from clinical presentation to scheduling/efficiency; it is largely determined by the case and sits between presentation and outcome, so it is a mediator rather than a confounder.

per_column.name: referral_or_consult_required
per_column.rationale: Referrals/consults are downstream consequences of the presentation that then affect scheduling flow; a mediator, not a common cause.

per_column.name: in_visit_procedure_performed
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure is performed is downstream of the clinical case and affects visit/scheduling load; lies on the causal path, so a mediator.

per_column.name: follow_up_interval_signal
per_column.rationale: Follow-up interval is an outcome of the visit that feeds subsequent scheduling; downstream, not a pre-treatment common cause.

per_column.name: patient_population_context
per_column.rationale: Patient demographic mix is a common cause of both case handling and efficiency; an immutable attribute, not an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: comorbidity_complexity_flag
per_column.rationale: Comorbidity complexity drives both triage prioritization and efficiency; a patient-intrinsic common cause, not settable.

judge.rationale: The query asks an interventional 'how can clinics improve' question, which requires an intervenable lever (e.g., staffing, appointment slot policy, triage protocol, walk-in vs scheduled, telehealth option) plus confounders adjusted for. NONE of the added columns is a settable treatment: they are all patient-/case-intrinsic characteristics or downstream mediators of the visit. Several columns (urgency signal, chief complaint, acuity, population, comorbidity) are plausible confounders, but a few of them merely echo existing columns (urgency, age_group, reason_for_visit) and thus are largely named/implied in the original context. Critically, no intervenable treatment exists, so the counterfactual 'what-if' cannot be set up. The what-if claim is not realised.
